role_summary: Translates research goals into concrete data specifications, RL environment designs, and evaluation frameworks that improve frontier model training. Owns the technical bridge between what researchers need and what the data/environment infrastructure produces.

capability_areas.name: Post-Training Data & RLHF Pipelines
capability_areas.description: Designing and building the data pipelines, reward models, and human feedback systems used to align and improve LLMs after pre-training.
builder_signals: Designed reward models or preference data collection systems
Built RLHF/DPO/PPO/GRPO training pipelines
Created data quality frameworks for human feedback
Published on alignment, reward modeling, or preference optimization
user_signals: Fine-tuned pre-trained models for business applications
Managed annotation teams without designing the annotation methodology
Deployed LLM-based products without training involvement

capability_areas.name: RL Environments & Verifier-Based Training
capability_areas.description: Building simulation environments, verifiers, and evaluation harnesses that test and train models through interaction rather than static data.
builder_signals: Built custom simulation environments for RL agent training
Designed verifier systems for automated evaluation
Created synthetic environment generators
Published on RL environment design or sim-to-real transfer
user_signals: Used OpenAI Gym / Stable Baselines for standard RL tasks
Applied RL to robotics control without designing the environment
Ran experiments in existing environments without modifying them

capability_areas.name: Coding Agent & SWE Agent Data
capability_areas.description: Building the datasets, benchmarks, and evaluation infrastructure for AI systems that write, debug, and test code autonomously.
builder_signals: Built or contributed to SWE-bench, HumanEval, MBPP, or similar benchmarks
Designed training data pipelines for code generation models
Created evaluation harnesses for coding agent performance
Published on neural program synthesis or code LLM training
user_signals: Used Copilot / ChatGPT for coding assistance
Built CI/CD pipelines or developer tools (standard SWE, not AI)
Applied code generation models to business problems

capability_areas.name: Multimodal & STEM Reasoning
capability_areas.description: Building training data, evaluation systems, and benchmarks for models that reason across modalities (vision, text, math, science).
builder_signals: Designed multimodal training datasets or benchmarks
Built evaluation frameworks for vision-language models
Created STEM reasoning datasets or evaluation harnesses
Published on VLMs, visual reasoning, or mathematical reasoning for LLMs
user_signals: Used vision APIs for image classification/detection in production
Applied OCR or document processing models
Built RAG systems with multimodal retrieval

capability_areas.name: Embodied AI & Simulation Infrastructure
capability_areas.description: Building the simulation infrastructure, synthetic data generation, and training environments for robots and physically-grounded AI systems.
builder_signals: Built simulation environments for robot training (Isaac Sim, PyBullet, MuJoCo)
Designed synthetic data generation pipelines for embodied agents
Created sim-to-real transfer frameworks
Published on embodied AI training, manipulation, or locomotion learning
user_signals: Used simulation tools for classical control validation only
Applied pre-trained vision models to robotics without training involvement
Did mechanical engineering or hardware design without ML training

depth_distinction.builder_definition: Designs training methodology, builds data/evaluation pipelines, creates environments or benchmarks, or conducts research that produces artifacts used to train or evaluate frontier models. The output of their work feeds into model training, not into a business application.
depth_distinction.user_definition: Fine-tunes or deploys pre-trained models for business use cases (fraud detection, recommendations, ad ranking, chatbots). Uses ML as a tool to solve business problems rather than building the infrastructure that makes models better.
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: MLOps/platform engineers who touch training infrastructure are borderline — save if their work directly enables model training (designed the training data pipeline, built the evaluation framework) but reject if they only manage the compute/deployment layer. Researchers at strong companies whose specific publications are in adjacent but non-target areas (e.g., NLP for information extraction, not for training data) should be evaluated on whether their methodology transfers, not whether their topic matches.

non_fit_patterns.label: Applied ML for business metrics
non_fit_patterns.description: ML engineers and data scientists building models that optimize business KPIs — fraud detection, credit scoring, churn prediction, recommendation engines, ad targeting, demand forecasting
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Strong ML practitioners but their work optimizes business outcomes, not model training quality. No connection to post-training data, RL environments, or evaluation systems.

non_fit_patterns.label: ML platform / MLOps without training
non_fit_patterns.description: Engineers who build deployment infrastructure, feature stores, model serving, A/B testing frameworks, or CI/CD for ML — but don't touch training data or model training
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Infrastructure adjacent to ML but not to the training/evaluation side. Their systems deploy models; they don't make models better.
examples: ML platform engineer managing Kubeflow clusters
Feature store architect at a fintech

non_fit_patterns.label: NLP application layer
non_fit_patterns.description: Engineers building chatbots, sentiment analysis, entity extraction, document processing, or search systems using pre-trained NLP models
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Uses language models as components in applications rather than building the training data, evaluation, or fine-tuning infrastructure for the models themselves.
examples: NLP engineer doing entity extraction for compliance

non_fit_patterns.label: Data engineering / ETL without training data design
non_fit_patterns.description: Engineers building data pipelines, warehouses, and ETL processes for analytics or business intelligence
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Moves and transforms data but doesn't design data for model training. 'Data' in their context means business data, not training data.
examples: Data engineer at a tech company building Spark pipelines

non_fit_patterns.label: Classical simulation without learned components
non_fit_patterns.description: Engineers doing CFD, FEA, circuit simulation, or other physics-based simulation without RL, learned models, or synthetic training data generation
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Simulation expertise that doesn't transfer to RL environment design or synthetic data for model training. 'Simulation' in their context is physics, not AI training.
examples: Aerospace simulation engineer doing flight dynamics
Chip design engineer using Monte Carlo simulation

non_fit_patterns.label: Annotation / data labeling operations
non_fit_patterns.description: People who manage or perform data annotation, labeling, or AI training tasks as an operational role rather than a research/engineering role
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Adjacent to training data but at the execution layer, not the design layer. The role requires someone who designs what gets annotated and how, not someone who performs the annotation.
examples: AI trainer at Scale AI or Turing

employer_signal_rules.evidence_required: Any evidence of working on model training, evaluation, or data quality. At frontier labs, even adjacent roles (research engineering, infrastructure) often touch training directly. Title + lab is strong but still need some signal of what they actually do.

Specific evidence of work in a capability area — team name, project description, publication, or skill keywords. Employer indicates they work around strong models, but many roles at these companies are application-layer.

Must show specific evidence of work in a capability area, not just 'ML at a strong company.' These companies have strong ML teams but most ML work there is applied (fraud, recommendations, pricing). Employer signal alone is NOT sufficient — this is the most common false positive source.
Same standard as any other candidate — capability area mapping + depth test. Unknown employer means the profile evidence carries all the weight.

minimum_bar_description: 4-5+ years hands-on building deep learning systems where data quality, model training, evaluation, or environment design was the primary output of their work — not a side effect of building a product. PhD research years count if the research involved building systems (not just analysis).

fast_exit_patterns: ENTIRE career is IT support, helpdesk, system administration — no ML/AI signal at any position
ENTIRE career is sales, business development, account management
ENTIRE career is HR, recruiting, people operations
ENTIRE career is pure management consulting with no technical implementation at any role
ENTIRE career is marketing, content creation, social media management
ENTIRE career is product management without technical ML work at any position
ENTIRE career is web development / frontend / mobile with no ML signal at any position
ENTIRE career is QA / manual testing without ML automation
trajectory_yes_patterns: Any position at a frontier AI lab (OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepMind, Meta FAIR, Microsoft Research) in a technical role
Career progression through ML research roles — Research Scientist/Engineer titles at multiple companies
Academic positions (PhD, postdoc, professor) with ML/AI affiliation visible in headline or education
Transitions from research/academia into industry ML roles — suggests research depth applied to practice
Any title containing 'RL', 'reinforcement learning', 'post-training', 'evaluation', 'training data', or 'simulation' at any position
trajectory_ambiguous_patterns: ML Engineer / Data Scientist at a strong tech company — could be applied ML or training infrastructure, CANNOT tell from snippet alone
Software Engineer at an AI company — could be product SWE or ML infrastructure
'AI' or 'ML' in headline but career history is mostly at non-AI companies — might be transitioning into the field
Mix of research and applied roles — trajectory direction unclear without job description bullets
Title says 'Senior' or 'Staff' ML at a known company but specific domain unknown from snippet
trajectory_no_patterns: ENTIRE career is data analytics / BI / reporting with no ML engineering positions at any point
ENTIRE career is traditional software engineering with no ML/AI/research signal across all positions
ENTIRE career is data engineering / ETL with no ML model training or research positions
ENTIRE career is IT infrastructure / DevOps / SRE with no ML signal
ENTIRE career is project/program management with no technical IC roles

author: Sam Vangelos
notes: Rebuilt from the OpenClaw campaign learnings. The general_tech employer tier is the most important calibration — Session 5's String #31 failure was caused by saving every ML engineer at Brazilian tech companies without requiring capability-area evidence.
